items.title: Treatment of Recurrent and/or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: CSCO and ASCO Joint Guideline
items.authors: Jiang W, Ismaila N, Chua ML, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To provide evidence-based recommendations on first- and subsequent-line systemic therapy, maintenance therapy, locoregional consolidation, and salvage local therapy for patients with recurrent and/or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Methods: A multidisciplinary Expert Panel convened by CSCO and ASCO reviewed evidence from randomized trials, meta-analyses, systematic reviews, prospective and retrospective studies, and clinical experience. The guideline was informed by a systematic literature review and consensus-based interpretation of efficacy, safety, feasibility, and patient-centered outcomes across scenarios. Outcomes included overall and progression-free survival, response and disease control rates, toxicity, and quality of life. Results: Evidence supports platinum-based chemotherapy plus a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor as preferred first-line therapy for medically fit patients. Evidence also supports maintenance strategies after disease control, while treatment selection depends on prior treatment, disease extent, patient fitness, resource availability, and preferences. Selected responders may receive locoregional consolidation radiotherapy or oral maintenance chemotherapy. For isolated locoregional recurrence amenable to local therapy, options include salvage surgery and re-irradiation. Recommendations: Chemotherapy plus a PD-1 inhibitor, followed by maintenance PD-1 inhibition for up to 2 years, should be offered first-line to appropriate patients with recurrent and/or metastatic NPC. Chemotherapy alone may be offered when immunotherapy is unsuitable or declined. Selected patients responding to first-line chemotherapy may receive oral maintenance chemotherapy or locoregional consolidation intensity-modulated radiotherapy. Salvage surgery or re-irradiation is recommended for appropriately selected patients with isolated locoregional recurrence. Subsequent-line options include chemotherapy, PD-1 inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates. Treatment should be individualized according to disease setting, prior therapy, expected toxicities, availability, local drug approvals, and patient preferences. Early supportive and specialist interdisciplinary palliative care, where available, should accompany active anticancer treatment for advanced, incurable disease.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/head-neck-cancer.

items.title: Supporting Contouring Education in Latin America: A Prospective Randomized Trial of Two Educational Approaches
items.authors: Dykstra MP, Cardozo PA, Calero O, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To facilitate increased adoption and quality of advanced radiation techniques in Latin America, upscaling provider contouring education is needed. The effectiveness of providing asynchronous learning materials versus learning materials plus synchronous education is unknown. We evaluated the efficacy of a remote, resident-led contouring curriculum. Methods And Materials: Residents and radiation oncologists from 2 public centers in Nicaragua and Paraguay were invited to enroll. Syllabus, lecture materials, and quiz questions were created based on contemporary standards for prostate, breast, gastrointestinal, gynecologic, and head and neck malignancies. Content was reviewed by expert U.S.-based radiation oncologists. All participants were asked to complete Test 1 prior to the curriculum launch. Then, all participants were provided access to lecture materials, guideline documents, and case examples. Center 1 also received 15 1-hour live remote lectures over 4 months delivered in Spanish by a U.S. senior radiation oncology resident, whereas Center 2 did not. After this 4-month period, both centers completed Test 2. Finally, Center 2 then received the same lecture series, and they alone took Test 3 afterward. Primary analysis was a 2-sided paired t test evaluating change from Test 1 to Test 2. Results: Twenty-one participants enrolled from Center 1 (n = 11, 100% staff participation) and Center 2 (n = 10, 71% staff participation), including 10 residents and 11 attending physicians. Mean Test 1 score was 57.0% (59.3% Center 1; 54.4% Center 2). Eleven participants completed Tests 1 and 2. Center 1 providers (n = 6) improved significantly between Tests 1 and 2 (64.4% versus 83.3%, P = .003), whereas those from Center 2 did not (55.1% versus 62.0%, P = .24). Center 2 providers (n = 9) improved from Test 1 to Test 3 (53.6% versus 74.1%, P = .001). Conclusions: A longitudinal, remote, resident-led contouring curriculum improved contouring knowledge more than provision of written resources alone and has potential for global scalability.

items.title: Treatment of Stage IB to III Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: CSCO-ASCO Guideline Update
items.authors: Chen YP, Ismaila N, Huang SH, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To update the 2021 CSCO-ASCO guideline on chemotherapy in combination with radiotherapy for the definitive treatment of non-metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), incorporating new evidence on radiotherapy techniques and target-volume de-escalation, chemotherapy regimens and their sequencing, adjuvant therapy, and immunotherapy for patients with stage IB-III disease. Methods: A multidisciplinary Expert Panel reviewed evidence published since the prior guideline, including randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant prospective and retrospective studies. Outcomes of interest included overall survival, failure-free or progression-free survival, locoregional and distant disease control, acute and late toxicities, and patient-reported quality of life. Recommendations were developed using the ASCO guideline development process and Expert Panel consensus. Results: The updated evidence supports: IMRT with image guidance and MRI-based target delineation as core components of definitive treatment; selected response-adapted target delineation following induction chemotherapy; elective nodal de-escalation in appropriately selected patients; risk-adapted chemotherapy sequencing according to stage and biologic risk; cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy; gemcitabine-cisplatin (GP) or docetaxel-cisplatin-fluorouracil (TPF) as preferred induction regimens; and selected adjuvant chemotherapy options, including metronomic capecitabine for patients with higher residual post-chemoradiotherapy risk. Several randomized trials evaluating PD-1 inhibitors have demonstrated improved disease-control outcomes, but overall survival data remain immature. Recommendations: This guideline update provides recommendations on radiotherapy technique, dose, imaging, and target delineation; sequencing of additional chemotherapy with radiotherapy; concurrent chemotherapy options; induction chemotherapy regimens and timing; adjuvant chemotherapy options; and the role of immunotherapy. At present, the Panel makes no recommendation for or against routine addition of immunotherapy to induction-concurrent chemoradiotherapy; applicability of the trial evidence, benefits and harms, local approval and access, and patient preferences should guide individualized decisions.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/head-neck-cancer.

items.title: Toxicity and patient-reported quality of life through 12 months following pelvis-inclusive once-weekly stereotactic body radiotherapy versus conventional IMRT for high-risk prostate cancer: updated results of the SRAM randomized phase II trial
items.authors: Poon DM, Wong KC, Lam DC, et al.
items.abstract: Aim: To compare toxicity through 12 months and patient-reported quality of life following pelvis-inclusive stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) versus conventional intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) in men with high-risk prostate cancer enrolled in the SRAM trial (NCT03938649). Methods: Men with node-negative high-risk prostate cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to pelvis-inclusive SBRT or IMRT. SBRT was delivered 40 Gy to the prostate and 25 Gy to the pelvis in five once-weekly fractions; IMRT comprised 50 Gy to the prostate and pelvis followed by a 26 Gy prostate boost. Gastrointestinal (GI) and genitourinary (GU) toxicities were graded using Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 4.0. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed using the Expanded Prostate Cancer Index (EPIC) and International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS). Results: Among 121 evaluable patients, 60 received SBRT and 61 IMRT. Between 6 and 12 months after radiotherapy, grade ≥2 GI and GU toxicity occurred in 16.7 % versus 13.1 % (p = 0.583) and 11.7 % versus 16.4 % (p = 0.455) of patients, respectively, including one grade 3 rectal hemorrhage after SBRT. EPIC bowel scores were lower in the SBRT group at 9 months (83.2 vs. 92.4; p = 0.0022) and 12 months (82.5 vs. 90.1; p = 0.0181), reflecting greater declines from baseline. Other EPIC domains and IPSS outcomes were broadly similar between groups. Conclusion: Once-weekly pelvis-inclusive SBRT showed no significant difference in grade ≥2 GI and GU toxicity compared with conventional IMRT at 6-12 months, but was associated with worse patient-reported bowel quality of life at 9-12 months.

items.title: Scenario-Based Simulation Teaching for Radiotherapy Plan Evaluation Using a Typical Defect Case Library: A Prospective, Multi-Center, Randomized Controlled Trial for Radiation Oncology Trainees
items.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.authors: Cao Y, Yang Z, Yang X
items.abstract: Purpose: The ability to evaluate radiotherapy plans is a core clinical decision-making competency for trainees in radiation oncology (RO). This study aims to evaluate, through a prospective, multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT), the effectiveness of scenario-based simulation teaching (SBST) using a typical defect case database compared to traditional lecture-based teaching in enhancing the treatment plan evaluation skills of RO trainees, and to analyze the impact of the pedagogical interventions on the trainees' cognitive psychological mechanisms. Methods: Forty RO trainees from three independent medical centers were enrolled and randomized into either the control (CON) or experimental (EXP) group. The CON group received traditional PowerPoint-based lectures focusing on standardized evaluation procedures and positive reference cases. The EXP group utilized the SBST model based on a typical defect case library, engaging in defect identification and feedback training within a high-fidelity plan evaluation environment. Primary endpoints included learning gains. Secondary endpoints encompassed cognitive load (NASA-TLX scale), multi-dimensional self-efficacy, and training satisfaction. Results: Both groups exhibited significant post-training improvements and the EXP group achieved significantly higher normalized learning gains than the CON group (p < 0.0001), with results demonstrating high consistency across all participating centers. Regarding cognitive load, while no significant differences were observed between the two groups in mental demand or extraneous load (interference burden) during either training or post-test stages, the EXP group experienced a statistically significant reduction in post-test frustration (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the EXP group outperformed the CON group across all dimensions of self-efficacy and training satisfaction. Conclusion: This prospective multi-center RCT demonstrates that the SBST model, based on a typical defect case library, is superior and highly scalable for enhancing the clinical practice skills of RO trainees. By bolstering core competency and professional confidence, this study provides robust evidence for integrating this model into standardized and homogeneous radiation oncologist training programs.

items.title: Prostate-specific antigen-based screening for prostate cancer: A systematic review to inform an American Cancer Society guideline
items.authors: Griffin JC, Shiau RL, Troutman CAB, et al.
items.abstract: Abstract The purpose of this systematic review was to identify and synthesize the evidence on the benefits and harms of prostate‐specific antigen (PSA)‐based screening for prostate cancer to inform the American Cancer Society’s updated guideline. PubMed and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for published and gray literature through December 4, 2023, and updated through October 29, 2025, which allowed for approximately 3 months of overlap with searches conducted for the previous guideline. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized comparisons of PSA‐based screening strategies to no screening or other screening strategies. Low– and medium–risk of bias systematic reviews were included, and their findings were supplemented with studies published after the systematic review. One investigator abstracted study data, and a second confirmed. Two investigators independently assessed the risk of bias and strength of evidence, and discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Twenty‐nine publications were included: two publications from a 2018 systematic review of PLCO, CAP, and ERSPC; 23 subsequent publications from six trials (PLCO, CAP, ERSPC, Göteborg‐1, Rotterdam Pilot 1, and ProScreen); and four observational studies. PSA‐based screening was associated with increased detection of low‐risk prostate cancer, reduced incidence of advanced or metastatic disease at diagnosis, and reduced cumulative incidence of metastatic disease. Screening was associated with a reduction in prostate cancer–specific mortality in some trials, although findings were inconsistent and likely depended on screening protocols, PSA thresholds, participant characteristics, and other factors. Harms of screening included overdiagnosis, false‐positive test results, biopsy‐related complications, and downstream treatment harms.

items.title: Symptom Monitoring With Patient-Reported Outcomes During Curative-Intent Radiation Treatment
items.authors: Raldow AC, Lee P, Chun SG, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Although symptom self-reporting improves clinical outcomes in patients with metastatic cancer receiving outpatient chemotherapy, the effects are not well established for patients undergoing radiation therapy (RT). In this randomized study, we assessed the impact of patient symptom self-reporting using the mobile Patient-Reported Outcomes version of the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events Administration system (mPROS) application during curative-intent RT with concurrent chemotherapy for gastrointestinal, gynecological, lung, central nervous system, and head and neck cancers on health-related quality of life. Methods And Materials: Enrolled patients were randomly assigned to symptom self-reporting with mPROS (experimental [EXP]) or usual care (control [CON]). EXP arm participants were asked to report symptoms at least weekly; severe or worsening symptoms triggered alerts to the clinical team. Participants remained in the study until 3 months after completion of RT. The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System - 29 (PROMIS-29) was administered at baseline, completion of RT (end-of-treatment [EOT]), and 3 months after RT completion. Patient assessment of the usefulness of mPROS was measured via a 24-question exit survey using a 7-point Likert scale. Results: There were 59 subjects enrolled, of which 55 (n = 28 EXP and n = 27 CON; mean age, 62.0 years; 69.1% male) completed at least 1 PROMIS-29. On average, EXP participants logged symptoms twice per week, with a mean of 15 severe attributes and 11 unique symptoms reported. There were no significant differences between mean changes in PROMIS-29 physical (EXP, ∆ -6.03 vs CON ∆ -4.04; P = .45) or mental (EXP ∆ -2.82 vs CON ∆ -2.17; P = .78) function scores from baseline to EOT. Likewise, there were no significant differences between median changes in PROMIS-29 physical (EXP ∆ -3.87 vs CON ∆ -2.22; P = .29) or mental (EXP ∆ -1.74 vs CON ∆ -1.39; P = .77) function scores from baseline to EOT. On multivariable linear regression adjusting for age, sex, race, ethnicity, and education, treatment arm was not a statistically significant predictor of physical [F(1,30) = 0.81; P = .38] or mental [F(1,30) = 0.00; P = .98] health scores at EOT. On the exit survey, mean scores for selected questions descriptively indicated high satisfaction and were as follows: care team understanding symptoms (6.27), feeling more involved in care (6.36), help with symptom tracking (6.18), and recommending mPROS to other patients (6.09).…

items.title: Early toxicity and dosimetry compliance of hypofractionated vs. conventional fractionated comprehensive regional nodes irradiation in breast cancer (HARVEST)
items.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.authors: Xu F, Huang X, Cai G, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: The HARVEST trial is a phase III randomized controlled trial comparing hypofractionated with conventional fractionated radiotherapy (HF-RT vs. CF-RT) with regional nodal irradiation (RNI, including internal mammary nodes [IMNs]) in breast cancer patients. In this study, we report the early toxicity profile, cosmetic outcomes and dosimetric quality assurance results. Methods And Analysis: Enrolled patients were randomized into the HF-RT group (40.05 Gy/15 Fx) or CF-RT group (50 Gy/25 Fx). Acute toxicity was assessed with the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) V.3.0 scale. Cosmetic outcome was assessed using the Harvard scale. Results: There were 400 and 401 patients enrolled in HF-RT and CF-RT group from eight centers in China, respectively. Protocol compliances exceeded 90% for most targets coverage and organs at risk constraint parameters in both groups, although IMN coverage was less complete than that of the chest wall/whole breast and supra/infraclavicular nodes. There was no significant difference of grade ≥ 2 acute toxicities between groups (RR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.52-1.22; p=0.29). Dermatitis was the most common acute toxicity, with a significantly lower rate of grade ≥ 2 events in the HF-RT group than in the CF-RT group (RR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.25-0.92; p=0.03). No significant differences were observed in other acute toxicities (including fatigue, pneumonitis, breast pain, dysphagia and breast edema) or in the proportion of good or excellent cosmesis among breast-conserving patients between groups. Conclusion: We found comparable acute toxicity and cosmesis results in HF-RT with RNI compared to CF-RT. The technical protocol was highly feasible with good protocol compliance. Additional follow-up is needed to assess the long-term efficacy and safety.

items.title: American Cancer Society guideline for the early detection of prostate cancer, 2026
items.authors: Hoffman RM, Wolf AMD, Etzioni RD, et al.
items.abstract: Abstract The goal of prostate cancer screening is to reduce morbidity and mortality through the early detection of clinically significant disease. Accumulating evidence shows that prostate‐specific antigen (PSA)‐based screening significantly reduces prostate cancer mortality and advanced‐stage diagnosis, and approaches to reduce harms associated with screening are increasingly being used. The ACS conducted a systematic review and commissioned a modeling study to evaluate PSA‐based screening strategies, and concluded that the benefits of screening outweigh the harms. Before initiating screening, clinicians should ensure that patients are informed about the benefits, limitations, and harms of screening; the potential follow‐up evaluations of elevated PSA levels; and the expectation that low‐risk cancers will initially be managed with active surveillance. The ACS recommends biennial screening from ages 50‐69 years for average‐risk men (i.e., non‐Black men without a family history of prostate cancer). Annual screening from ages 45‐69 years is recommended for Black men. Annual screening from ages 45–69 years is recommended for non‐Black men with a strong family history (i.e., multiple first‐degree relatives diagnosed with prostate cancer at any age or one diagnosed before age 65 years). Biennial screening from ages 45‐69 years is recommended for non‐Black men with a single first‐degree relative diagnosed at age 65 years or older. For men ages 70–74 years, the balance of benefits and harms is uncertain, and individualized decision making is recommended. The ACS recommends further evaluating men ages 45–69 years with PSA levels ≥3.0 ng/mL and men ages 70–74 years with PSA levels ≥6.5 ng/mL. Most men who have elevated PSA levels confirmed on repeat testing should be offered magnetic resonance imaging and/or a validated biomarker test to guide biopsy decisions. Screening is not recommended for men with a life expectancy <10 years and should be discontinued at age 75 years.

items.title: Nivolumab and total neoadjuvant treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer: results of a phase II trial (CA209-8M4)
items.authors: Brenner B, Perl G, Rosenberg-Ayal A, et al.
items.abstract: Background: CA209-8M4 is a prospective phase II trial evaluating the addition of nivolumab to total neoadjuvant treatment (TNT) in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). Materials And Methods: Patients with LARC (T3-4Nany or TanyN1) up to 12 cm from the anal verge received standard chemoradiation (CRT) followed by chemoimmunotherapy (CIMT): six cycles of standard mFOLFOX6 and nivolumab at 240 mg. We defined a novel primary endpoint, combining pathological complete response (pCR) rate among operated patients and long-term (≥12 months) clinical complete response (cCR) rate for those electing watchful waiting, into a composite endpoint of modified pCR (mpCR) rate. Results: Between April 2019 and March 2024, 29 patients were enrolled, median age 53 years, 72.4% male; 96.6% of tumors were cT3 or cT4, 69.0% cN+, and 96.6% microsatellite stable. Median distance from the anal verge was 7 cm; 51.7% of patients had grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) during CIMT, including one fatality (mesenteric inflammation), attributed most likely to CRT's unresolved toxicity. Immune-mediated AEs occurred in four patients (13.8%): grade 3 diabetes mellitus (1) and grade 1 hepatitis (3), including one with asymptomatic hyper/hypothyroidism. Twenty-eight patients (96.6%) are assessable for mpCR: 6 of the 15 operated achieved pCR, and 13 were not operated with cCR ≥12 months, leading to a 67.9% mpCR rate. With a median follow-up of 43.5 months (range 25.0-84.1+), all 28 assessable pts are alive with no evidence of disease. The estimated 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival rates of the entire group are 93% [95% confidence interval (CI) 84-100] and 97% (95% CI 90-100), respectively. Conclusions: The addition of nivolumab to standard TNT in LARC seems safe and may enhance its effectiveness, with encouraging mpCR and survival rates. A multicenter randomized trial, further evaluating this strategy, is ongoing.

items.title: Impact of Metastatic Spine Score on Optimizing Enrollment Selectivity on a Multicenter Phase Two Randomized Controlled Trial
items.authors: McClelland S 3rd
items.abstract: Objectives: A key barrier to successful trial completion is that enrolled patients do not reach the trial's primary endpoint timeframe. This study examines the impact of a heuristic algorithm on screening patients who are otherwise at high risk for primary endpoint failure in a trial that has recently completed enrollment. Methods: The Spine Patient Optimal Radiosurgery Treatment for Symptomatic Metastatic Neoplasms (SPORTSMEN) multicenter Phase II randomized controlled trial examines the impact of radiation therapy on pain freedom in metastatic spine disease, with a primary endpoint of pain freedom at 3 months post-treatment. The rate of enrollment failure due to predicted inadequate prognosis (<3 mo) was compared before versus after implementation of the Metastatic Spine Score to assess the impact of this algorithm on trial enrollment. Results: A total of 136 patients were evaluated for trial enrollment. The first 64 patients were evaluated before the implementation of the Metastatic Spine Score, of whom 1 (2%) was excluded from enrollment due to an inadequate prognosis. The final 72 patients were evaluated after implementation of the Metastatic Spine Score; 15 patients (21%) were excluded from enrollment due to an inadequate prognosis. This difference in exclusion rate was statistically significant (P=0.0003). Conclusions: In conclusion, the implementation of a heuristic algorithm during clinical trial enrollment had a significant impact on the prohibition of enrollment of patients at increased risk of primary endpoint failure. These results serve as a reminder of the importance of objectively quantifying prognosis and its impact on the risk of primary endpoint failure.

items.title: Early vs Routine Oral Nutritional Supplementation During Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial
items.authors: Su L, Bai ZG, Liu RQ, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Oral nutritional supplementation (ONS), providing supplementary oral nutrition in addition to usual food, is widely used during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), but its optimal timing and cost utility remain uncertain. Objective: To evaluate efficacy and explore cost utility of early ONS in patients with NPC undergoing CCRT. Design, Setting, And Participants: This multicenter, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 6 Chinese tertiary hospitals from July 2021 to May 2025. Eligible patients were aged 18 to 70 years with newly diagnosed stage II to IVA NPC, a Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA) score of 0 to 8, and planned CCRT. Key exclusions included oral intake less than 60% of requirements for 3 days or longer, inability or unwillingness to receive concurrent chemotherapy, and inability to receive oral or enteral nutrition. Data were analyzed from November 2025 to March 2026. Intervention: Participants were randomized 1:1 to early ONS at CCRT start or routine ONS after prespecified nutritional decline. Main Outcomes And Measures: The primary end point was the incidence of more than 5% weight loss from baseline to CCRT completion. Secondary end points included PG-SGA score, the incidence of grade 3 or higher radiation-induced oral mucositis (RIOM), quality of life (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30), and radiotherapy interruption. Cost utility measures included total cost, utility, and incremental cost utility ratio. Results: Of 242 patients screened, 236 patients were randomized, and the prespecified modified intention-to-treat population included 216 patients (mean [SD] age, 46.62 [11.19] years; 168 [77.8%] male), with 107 receiving early ONS and 109 receiving routine ONS. More than 5% weight loss occurred in 70 participants (65.4% ) in the early ONS group, compared with 88 participants (80.7%) in the routine ONS group (relative risk [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.96; P = .01). An intention-to-treat analysis including all randomized participants yielded a similar estimate (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.65-0.93). In the modified intention-to-treat population, grade 3 or higher RIOM occurred in 15 participants (14.0%) in the early ONS group vs 29 participants (26.6%) in the routine ONS group (RR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.30-0.93). Best-case costs were $9560.56 in the early ONS group vs $9685.23 in the routine ONS group, with quality-adjusted life-years of 0.1144 vs 0.1132, respectively.…

items.title: Transarterial Chemoembolization and Chemo-Immunoembolization in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: An Updated Systematic Review
items.authors: Saadeh OA, Temperley HC, O'Sullivan NJ, et al.
items.abstract: Locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) often requires aggressive multimodal therapy, yet pathological complete response (pCR) to standard chemoradiotherapy remains low. Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) enables targeted locoregional delivery of chemotherapy to tumor-feeding arteries, and its recent extension, chemo-immunoembolization, permits intraarterial delivery of immune checkpoint inhibitors. This updated systematic review searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science from inception to June 2026 for studies of TACE or transcatheter rectal arterial chemoembolization (TRACE) in LARC, with quality appraised using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Nine studies encompassing 822 patients, 582 of whom received TACE or TRACE, were included, predominantly from China; one further trial is ongoing. pCR rates ranged from 10% to 44.74%. In comparative studies, TRACE with oxaliplatin was associated with lower tumor regression grade 3 (TRG3) rates, reaching significance in the largest comparison, and with a survival benefit in an exploratory TRG3 subgroup analysis, suggesting a possible role in chemoradiotherapy-resistant disease. The highest pCR occurred in a phase II trial of intra-arterial tislelizumab plus TACE in mismatch repair-proficient LARC, with no grade 3-4 immune-related adverse events. Major complications were uncommon. TACE may improve pathological response with an acceptable safety profile in LARC, although comparative evidence is limited and non-randomized; CIETAI provides first-in-human proof-of-concept for intra-arterial delivery of immunotherapy.

items.title: Addition of tucatinib to trastuzumab/pertuzumab after local therapy for isolated intracranial progression in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer: primary results of the phase II BRIDGET trial
items.authors: Sammons SL, Van Swearingen AED, Bagegni NA, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Brain metastases are common in advanced human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer, often with stable extracranial disease. Current guidelines for isolated intracranial progression recommend local therapy followed by continuation of the same systemic regimen, given the absence of data supporting a change in therapy. BRIDGET tested whether adding tucatinib, a central nervous system (CNS)-active, HER2-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor, to an ongoing HER2-targeted backbone prevents further intracranial progression after isolated CNS relapse. Materials And Methods: Secondary BRain metastases prevention after Isolated intracranial progression on Trastuzumab/Pertuzumab or T-DM1 in patients with aDvanced human epidermal Growth factor receptor 2+ brEast cancer with the addition of Tucatinib (BRIDGET) is a single-arm, phase II trial (NCT05323955) enrolling patients with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer experiencing a first or second isolated intracranial event with stable/absent extracranial disease while on trastuzumab/pertuzumab (TP) or ado-trastuzumab emtansine. All new or progressive brain lesions >5 mm underwent stereotactic radiosurgery before enrollment. Tucatinib 300 mg b.i.d. was added continuously to anti-HER2 antibody backbone therapy. The primary endpoint was intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS) per Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Brain Metastases. The study was designed to distinguish a 3-month improvement in PFS to >8.0 months versus a historical control median of 5.0 months by one-sample log-rank test (one-sided α = 0.05; 90% power). Results: Of 48 patients, 47 were eligible and assessable (median age 53.5 years; 97.9% female; 93.6% on backbone TP). At a median follow-up of 19.6 months, the study met its primary endpoint: median iPFS was not reached and significantly exceeded the prespecified historical control estimate of 5.0 months (P < 0.0001). 12- and 18-month iPFS estimates were 64% [95% confidence interval (CI) 48-76] and 59% (95% CI 42-73). Extracranial progression was rare (2 patients, 4.3%), and overall survival was exceptional (46 of 47 patients alive). items.title: Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy with Modern Bowel-Sparing Intensity-Modulated Radiotherapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Multicenter Single-Arm Phase II Trial
items.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.authors: Sakanaka K, Hida K, Ito D, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: The study evaluated the risk of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea of modern bowel-sparing intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT)-based neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) versus three-dimensional conformal radiotherapy (3DCRT)-based nCRT. Materials And Methods: In this open-label, historically controlled, multicenter, single-arm phase II trial, patients with LARC, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2, and adequate organ function were recruited. Protocol treatment involved concurrent capecitabine and IMRT, consisting of 45 Gy (25 fractions) for elective nodes and an optional 5.4 Gy (3 fractions) boost for gross disease. Bowel-sparing constraints included small-bowel volume receiving 15 Gy (V15Gy) of <200 cc. Acute toxicities were graded in the protocol-defined primary outcome window. Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea was tested against a 26% historical benchmark from phase II trials of 3DCRT-based nCRT with capecitabine with a one-sided α-level of 0.05 and 80% power. Results: Fifty-five patients were enrolled, including 48 patients with stage III disease and 25 patients with a positive circumferential resection margin on magnetic resonance imaging. Fifty-four patients (98.2%) completed protocol-defined nCRT. The median small-bowel V15Gy was 85 cc (interquartile range, 47-105). Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea occurred in four patients (7.3%; 90% confidence interval, 2.5-15.9; p < 0.001) in the intention-to-treat cohort. Fifty patients underwent radical surgery, and the pathological complete response and circumferential resection margin >1 mm rates were 6.0% and 88.0%, respectively, with grade ≥2 postoperative complications observed in 14% of patients. After median follow-up of 14 months, the 12-month locoregional progression-free and overall survival rates were 95.0% and 98.2%, respectively. Conclusions: Modern bowel-sparing IMRT in nCRT for LARC was associated with a low rate of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea with no obvious unfavorable signals for resectability, locoregional control, or safety; however, longer follow-up is needed to assess mature oncologic outcomes and late toxicities.

items.title: Surgical management of cervical cancer: A Society of Gynecologic Oncology evidence-based review
items.authors: Melamed A, Covens AL, Pfaendler KS, et al.
items.abstract: Surgical management of cervical cancer has changed substantially over the past decade as randomized and prospective data have refined the extent of resection, the role of fertility-sparing surgery, nodal assessment strategies, and the choice of surgical approach. This Society of Gynecologic Oncology evidence-based review addresses the upfront surgical management of cervical cancer. Surgery for recurrent disease, including pelvic exenteration and resection of oligometastatic recurrence, is outside its scope. A panel of gynecologic oncologists and subject matter experts identified twelve clinical questions spanning extent of resection, fertility-sparing surgery, lymph node assessment, surgical approach, and the integration of surgery with chemoradiation. Relevant literature was systematically collected and synthesized, and each recommendation was assigned a strength of recommendation and quality of evidence using a two-part rating system adapted from the ASCCP guidelines. Recommendations were approved by the SGO Clinical Practice Committee, Document Review Panel, and Board of Directors. Simple hysterectomy with nodal assessment is preferred for low-risk FIGO 2018 stage IA through IB1 disease. Fertility-sparing surgery is acceptable for appropriately selected patients with low-risk stage IA1 through IB1 tumors, with conization or simple trachelectomy preferred over radical trachelectomy. Sentinel lymph node biopsy may replace complete pelvic lymphadenectomy when an accepted algorithm is applied, with indocyanine green and near-infrared imaging the preferred mapping technique. When radical hysterectomy is indicated, the open approach is preferred outside of a clinical trial. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery is not recommended in place of chemoradiation, and hysterectomy after completion of definitive chemoradiation is not recommended in the absence of documented residual disease. Evidence quality varies considerably across questions, and several recommendations rest on observational data or expert consensus.

items.title: Integrating Chemotherapy With Immunotherapy Prior to Surgery for Patients With Locally Advanced HNSCC
items.abstract: In JAMA Oncology, Liu et al present the results of the phase 2 CAMORAL randomized clinical trial, demonstrating an event-free survival (EFS) benefit for neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (carboplatin/paclitaxel combined with camrelizumab; 2 cycles) and maintenance camrelizumab (15 cycles) added to standard of care (SOC) compared to SOC alone in locally advanced, surgically resectable stage III/IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC). This regimen was associated with a significant improvement in the primary end point of investigator-assessed 2-year EFS (77.8%; 95% CI, 63.6%-87.0%) compared to SOC (2-year EFS, 46.1%; 95% CI, 31.3%-59.6%; stratified hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.17-0.68; P = .001). Importantly, despite higher rates of treatment-related adverse events in the experimental arm (any grade, 79.4% vs 56.5%; grade ≥3, 20.6% vs 16.1%), the percentage of patients who proceeded to surgery were similar in both groups (92.1% vs 91.9%). Surgical delays were more common in the experimental arm (17.2% vs 0%), although delays in the experimental group were predominantly attributed to COVID-19–related factors.

items.title: Perioperative Camrelizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial
items.authors: Liu F, Zhang Y, Ma H, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Despite multimodal treatment, recurrence remains common in patients with resectable locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Whether perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improves long-term outcomes remains uncertain. Objective: To estimate the effect of perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy on event-free survival (EFS) compared with standard surgery-based treatment in patients with resectable locally advanced HNSCC. Design, Setting, And Participants: The CAMORAL trial was a multicenter, phase 2 randomized clinical trial conducted at 4 academic hospitals in China between October 2020 and March 2024, with data cutoff on April 11, 2025. Patients aged 18 to 75 years with untreated, resectable stage III to IVB HNSCC were assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant treatment or control. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Data were analyzed from May 2025 to February 2026. Interventions: Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive two 21-day cycles of neoadjuvant camrelizumab, 200 mg, plus albumin-bound paclitaxel and carboplatin followed by surgery, risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, and maintenance camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles; or upfront surgery followed by standard risk-adapted adjuvant therapy. Main Outcomes And Measures: The primary end point was 2-year EFS. Secondary end points included major pathological response (MPR), pathological complete response (pCR), overall survival, 2-year distant metastasis-free survival, 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival, and safety. Results: Of 125 included patients, 99 (79.2%) were male, and the mean (SD) age was 56.3 (11.7) years. A total of 63 patients were assigned to the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 62 to the control group; the median (IQR) follow-up was 24.6 (16.8-36.5) months. A total of 103 (82.4%) had oral cavity primary tumors. Among 125 patients, the 2-year EFS rate was 77.8% (95% CI, 63.6-87.0) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group compared with 46.1% (95% CI, 31.3-59.6) in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.17-0.68; P = .001). MPR and pCR were 47.6% (95% CI, 34.9-60.6) and 25.4% (95% CI, 15.3-37.9), respectively, in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group, with no MPR or pCR events in the control group. The 2-year overall survival rates were 92.0% and 69.1%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.10-0.64); the hazard ratio of 2-year distant metastasis-free survival was 0.15 (95% CI, 0.03-0.68).…

items.title: Navigating treatment for De novo oligometastatic breast cancer: The Assisi think tank meeting
items.authors: Felice F, Pedretti S, Palumbo I, et al.
items.abstract: The 2026 Assisi Think Tank Meeting, in collaboration with EUSOMA, ESTRO, and AIRO, identified de novo oligometastatic breast cancer (dnOMBC) as a clinically relevant challenge. A comprehensive review of 39 publications highlights a significant heterogeneity in locoregional treatment strategies, including varying approaches to surgical and radiation oncology management for both the primary tumour as for the metastases. The overall level of evidence is low, with only one trial, MF07-01, demonstrating a clear benefit in terms of overall survival. Therefore, we recommend applying the Advanced Breast Cancer (ABC) guidelines, considering locoregional interventions after a 3-8 months induction of systemic therapy to facilitate identification of patients with better outcomes. On longer term perspective, our findings emphasise the need for obtaining more results from ongoing and future prospective clinical trials to define the optimal role of local therapies, including surgery and radiation therapy, in improving patient outcomes. For this, we encourage a proper application of biologically driven paradigms, using advanced imaging and biomarker monitoring to better identify true oligometastatic disease, as well as to optimise outcomes by combining locoregional treatments with immunotherapy.

items.title: Dasatinib Dose Optimization With Weekend Drug Holiday for Improved Tolerability in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (DasaHIT): A German Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Alliance Randomized Trial
items.authors: La Rosée P, Ernst P, Fabisch C, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To compare standard-dose dasatinib 100 mg once daily with reduced-dose using a weekend drug holiday to improve tolerability for patients with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). Patients And Methods: Patients with chronic phase CML (CP-CML) were randomly assigned to either receive standard-of-care dasatinib 100 mg once daily or an intermittent dasatinib schedule (5 days on, 2 days [weekend] off) in a prospective multicenter phase III trial. Achievement of major molecular remission (MMR) at 24 months and a newly developed cumulative toxicity score were coprimary end points. Results: Of 289 eligible patients, 147 were assigned to standard-of-care dasatinib and 142 to intermittent dosing. Eighty percent of patients received first-line treatment (n = 232). In the standard arm, 105 of 130 patients (81% [95% CI, 74% to 88%) achieved MMR at 24 months compared with 101 of 130 patients (78% [95% CI, 71% to 85%]) in the experimental arm resulting in noninferiority within the prespecified noninferiority margin of 15% (P = .009). Among second- or later-line patients, MMR at 24 months was 24% lower, failing noninferiority. Comparison of grade 2-4 toxicities revealed no significant difference between the treatment arms. However, a post hoc analysis of toxicities of special interest (pleural effusion/pericardial effusion) showed 21 of 130 patients (16%) in the standard arm versus 10 of 125 (8%) patients in the experimental arm (P = .0464). Consistently, health-related quality of life improved mainly in first-line patients, with more favorable outcomes in the experimental arm. Conclusion: Intermittent dasatinib dosing with weekend treatment holidays in patients with CP-CML is noninferior to continuous dosing with respect to MMR at 24 months, at least in the first-line setting. The incidence of pleural or pericardial effusion appears to be reduced compared with standard-of-care continuous dosing.

items.title: Olanzapine or prochlorperazine added to antiemetic therapy for persistent chemotherapy-induced nausea: an NCORP phase 3 RCT
items.authors: Peppone LJ, Morrow GR, Alieldin R, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Despite guideline-consistent antiemetic prophylaxis, persistent chemotherapy-induced nausea remains common, and comparative phase 3 evidence for olanzapine versus prochlorperazine is limited. We evaluated whether adding olanzapine or prochlorperazine to standardized Cycle 2 antiemetic prophylaxis reduces persistent nausea compared with placebo. Methods: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 23 NCORP community oncology sites (April 2018-January 2024), women 18 years or older with breast cancer receiving moderately or highly emetogenic chemotherapy who recorded a Cycle 1 nausea score of 3 or greater (1-7 scale) were randomized 1:1:1 during Cycle 2 to placebo, prochlorperazine (10 mg every 8 hours, Days 1-4), or olanzapine (10 mg once daily, Days 1-4), added to netupitant/palonosetron plus dexamethasone. The primary outcome was change in average nausea from Cycle 1 to Cycle 2; the key secondary outcome was change in maximum nausea. Results: Among 1363 screened patients, 310 comprised the intention-to-treat population (placebo, 91; prochlorperazine, 110; olanzapine, 109). Compared with placebo, average nausea improved with prochlorperazine (between-group difference, -0.44; P=.01) and olanzapine (-0.57; P=.001). Olanzapine reduced maximum nausea more than prochlorperazine (difference, -0.59; P=.02) and improved FACT-G quality-of-life scores over placebo (difference, 4.91; P=.006) and prochlorperazine (5.80; P=.001). Adverse events were primarily grade 1-2, with no toxicity-related discontinuations. Conclusions: Adding olanzapine or prochlorperazine to standardized Cycle 2 antiemetic prophylaxis reduced persistent chemotherapy-induced nausea compared with placebo. Olanzapine produced greater improvement in maximum nausea and quality of life than prochlorperazine and is an effective escalation option, with prochlorperazine a reasonable alternative when olanzapine is unsuitable. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03367572.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Adjuvant Single-Fraction Radiotherapy for Excised Keloids: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial
items.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.authors: Roan TL, Chang DH, Kuo DY, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: While fractionated postoperative radiotherapy regimens for keloids are well established, the optimal dose for single-fraction delivery remains to be definitively defined. This prospective, randomized trial characterized the dose-response relationship of single-fraction radiotherapy and evaluated the impact of local tissue tension on treatment outcomes. Methods And Materials: Eighty-eight patients with surgically excised keloids were randomized to receive a single fraction of electron beam radiotherapy at 9 Gy (n = 30), 11 Gy (n = 29), and 13 Gy (n = 29) within 24 hours of surgery. The primary endpoint was 12-month local control. Secondary endpoints included objective scar assessment using the modified Vancouver Scar Scale (mVSS) and patient-reported quality of life via Skindex-16. Results: At 12 months, recurrence rates were 23.3%, 17.2%, and 6.9% for the 9, 11, and 13 Gy groups, respectively. In multivariable logistic regression, the 9 Gy dose was an independent predictor of recurrence relative to 13 Gy (OR, 5.7; 95% CI, 1.0-32.3; P = .046). Longitudinal analysis using generalized estimating equations demonstrated superior objective scar outcomes in the 13 Gy group compared with 9 Gy (P < .001) and 11 Gy (P < .001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an mVSS score ≥ 7 as a highly accurate predictor of recurrence (AUC = 0.93). Conclusions: A 13 Gy single-fraction postoperative regimen provided superior local control and cosmetic outcomes compared with 9 Gy, particularly at high-tension anatomic sites. These findings support a risk-stratified, tension-based dosing strategy, wherein dose de-escalation may be considered at low-tension sites without compromising local control.

items.abstract: Obtaining maximal conformality is of utmost importance in the definitive treatment of oropharyngeal cancer given the high toxicity associated with treatment. Both intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT)/volumetric modulated arc therapy and proton therapy are standards of care in patients requiring bilateral neck treatment. Randomized evidence suggests an improvement in acute toxicity but smaller differences in late toxicity with proton therapy. If proton therapy is readily available with sufficient capacity, we lean toward recommending that, however, we are comfortable recommending either treatment option.

items.title: Longitudinal dynamics and recovery of lymphocytes in patients with breast cancer receiving radiotherapy without chemotherapy after breast-conserving surgery: A second analysis of a phase III randomized trial of HYPOfractionation in BREAST radiotherapy for Chinese women (CHN HYPOBREAST)
items.authors: Song YC, Zhang CN, Sun GY, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Radiotherapy-induced lymphopenia (RIL) has been associated with inferior clinical outcomes in multiple solid tumors. However, the long-term dynamics and recovery of peripheral lymphocyte counts (PLCs) after radiotherapy remain poorly characterized. Objectives: To evaluate the longitudinal dynamics of PLCs in patients with breast cancer treated with radiotherapy (RT) without chemotherapy after breast-conserving surgery (BCS) and to identify the timepoint of recovery to pre-treatment levels. Design: A secondary analysis of PLC dynamics was performed in selected patients enrolled in the prospective, multicenter, randomized phase III CHN-HYPOBREAST trial comparing hypofractionated RT (HFRT) with conventional fractionated RT (CFRT) after BCS. Methods: This study included 203 patients. Among them, 96 were in the HFRT group and 107 were in the CFRT group. PLCs were measured at baseline (before any cancer treatment), pre-RT (after surgery but before RT), weekly during RT, and periodically up to 5 years after RT. Longitudinal PLC trends were analyzed using generalized linear mixed models. Results: The pre-RT PLCs were comparable to baseline, and the PLCs gradually decreased during RT. In the HFRT and CFRT groups, the PLCs recovered to the baseline level 3 and 4 years after RT, respectively. Compared with the CFRT group, the HFRT group had a significantly higher mean nadir PLC (1.26 ± 0.42 × 109/L vs. 1.05 ± 0.32 × 109/L, P < 0.001) and a significantly lower ≥G2 lymphopenia rate (6.5% vs. 24.5%, P = 0.001). Conclusions: RT-induced lymphopenia in patients with breast cancer undergoing BCS without chemotherapy was generally mild. HFRT resulted in less severe lymphopenia than CFRT. However, the PLCs experienced a prolonged reduction period in both groups, recovering to baseline level 3 years after RT with HFRT and 4 years with CFRT. These findings provide additional evidence supporting the clinical use of HFRT and highlight the need for strategies to minimize RIL and promote lymphocyte recovery.

items.title: ESTRO consensus recommendations: target volume and organ at risk delineation in rectal endoluminal high dose rate brachytherapy
items.authors: Valkenburg AC, Van Limbergen EJ, Knoth J, et al.
items.abstract: Background And Purpose: Lack of international guidelines is hampering treatment quality and progress in the field of rectal endoluminal high dose rate brachytherapy (EHB). Standardisation of dose reporting would allow for better comparison of clinical results between patient cohorts and allow tumour control and normal tissue complication probability modelling. This work presents consensus recommendations for target volume and organs at risk (OAR) delineation in rectal EHB to support standardised dose reporting, for which consistent delineation is a prerequisite. Materials And Methods: Recommendations were developed according to the AGREE II instrument, using a modified Delphi approach. The process included selection of international experts, a survey on current practices, delineation of three patient cases, and three consensus meetings to discuss the findings and formulate recommendations. Results: The expert group included 30 members from nine countries. The survey and first delineation round showed marked variation in treatment preparation and in the definition and delineation of target volumes and OARs. Consensus was reached on prerequisites for adequate delineation. Target volumes for dose reporting were defined: GTV primary at the time of EHB (GTVp_BT), an evaluation structure (GTVp_BT_ev05), and any macroscopic lymph nodes at the time of EHB (GTVn_BT). Recommendations for OAR selection and delineation were also established. Conclusion: The GI GEC working group of GEC-ESTRO has developed consensus recommendations for target volume definition and OAR delineation in rectal EHB. These recommendations will be implemented in clinical practice. The proposed structures provide a foundation for standardised dose reporting, independent of local prescription practices.

items.title: Circulating Tumor DNA in Oligoprogressive Prostate Cancer Treated With Stereotactic Radiotherapy: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of a Nonrandomized Clinical Trial
items.authors: Reid A, Tran A, Thakali S, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is increasingly used for oligoprogressive prostate cancer, but the duration of disease control is highly variable. Objective: To evaluate time to progression based on circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) prior to SBRT. Design, Setting, And Participants: Between October 17, 2018, and February 1, 2023, the phase 2 prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized clinical TRAP (Targeted Radiotherapy in Androgen-Suppressed Prostate Cancer Patients) trial evaluated SBRT to treat 81 patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and 2 or fewer metastases and imaging evidence of progression while receiving an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI). Plasma DNA was collected at 1 or 2 points prior to SBRT and centrally tested for ctDNA using the next-generation sequencing assay PCF_SELECT. Data were collected prospectively using electronic trial case report forms. Data were extracted November 26, 2025. The median follow-up was 24.5 (IQR, 23.7-36.3) months. Exposures: Progressing metastases were treated with SBRT, and patients were followed up with clinical assessments, serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) tests, and imaging. Main Outcomes And Measures: The primary outcome measure was time to progression, defined as an increase in serum prostate-specific antigen level of 25% or greater from the post-SBRT nadir, radiologic or symptomatic progression, clinician decision to stop ARPI, or death from any cause. The secondary outcomes were time to next therapy or death from any cause. All end points were measured from time of final SBRT treatment. Results: Of 77 patients with evaluable blood samples taken prior to SBRT, 19 (24.7%) were in the ctDNA-positive group. The 6-month progression-free survival (PFS) rate was 21.1% (95% CI, 6.6%-41.0%) for the ctDNA-positive group compared with 58.3% (95% CI, 44.5%-69.8%) for the ctDNA-negative group. The median PFS was 3.0 (95% CI, 2.7-5.9) months for the ctDNA-positive group and 7.8 (95% CI, 5.9-11.4) months for the ctDNA negative group (log rank test, P = .003 at 5% significance level). The median time to initiation of a new therapy or death was 15.3 (95% CI, 4.7-26.0) months for the ctDNA-positive group and 29.6 (95% CI, 17.8-37.6) months for the ctDNA-negative group. The median overall survival was 27.2 (95% CI, 19.2 to undefined) months for the ctDNA-positive group and 33.6 (95% CI, 28.4-38.2) months for the ctDNA-negative group.…

items.title: Dosimetric comparison of wedge, field-in-field, IMRT, VMAT and hybrid radiotherapy techniques: A systematic review
items.authors: Afrianti E, Tahir D, Astuty SD
items.abstract: Background: Radiotherapy is a key modality in cancer treatment, requiring a balance between sufficient dose delivery to the Planning Target Volume (PTV) and minimizing radiation exposure to surrounding organs at risk (OAR). The evolution of techniques from wedge-based conventional planning to Field-in-Field (FIF), Intensity-Modulated Radiotherapy (IMRT), Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (VMAT), and most recently, hybrid planning aims to improve dose homogeneity, conformity, and treatment efficiency. Objective: To systematically compare dosimetric performance among wedge, FIF, IMRT, VMAT, and hybrid techniques in terms of dose homogeneity (HI), conformity (CI), PTV coverage, OAR sparing, and monitor unit (MU) efficiency. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Articles were retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar (2015-2025). Studies were included if they reported comparison of ≥2 techniques and provided dosimetric parameters (HI, CI, PTV coverage, OAR dose, and/or MU). There are 25 eligible studies covering breast, prostate, head and neck, rectal, lung, and whole-brain radiotherapy were analyzed. Results: FIF consistently demonstrated better dose homogeneity and reduced hotspots than wedge techniques. IMRT and VMAT improved conformity and PTV coverage, with VMAT offering higher delivery efficiency due to lower MU requirements. Hybrid techniques combining FiF/3DCRT with IMRT or VMAT provided the most balanced outcomes: improved HI and CI, reduced low-dose spread, and lower OAR exposure, particularly to heart and ipsilateral lung in left-sided breast irradiation. Conclusion: Hybrid radiotherapy represents the optimal compromise between dosimetric quality, OAR protection, and treatment efficiency. FIF is superior to wedge for simple geometries, VMAT is preferred for complex targets, and hybrid techniques are recommended when both conformity and OAR sparing are critical.

items.title: Prognostic value of lymph node ratio beyond extranodal extension in node-positive oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma
items.authors: Kumar A, Laskar SG, Sharma P, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Extranodal extension (ENE) is a key determinant of adjuvant therapy in node-positive oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). However, conventional nodal staging may not fully capture the quantitative burden of nodal disease. We evaluated whether lymph node ratio (LNR) provides additional prognostic value beyond ENE in a large randomized trial cohort. Methods And Materials: We performed a retrospective subgroup analysis of 661 node-positive patients from the phase III randomized Oral Cavity Adjuvant Therapy (OCAT) trial. LNR was defined as the metastatic-to-dissected lymph node ratio and categorized as low (<0.10) or high (≥0.10). Overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and locoregional control (LRC) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression, adjusting for ENE, T stage, N stage, PNI, margin status, LVI, and treatment arm. Results: With a median follow-up of 91 months, 387 deaths occurred. On multivariable analysis, high LNR remained independently associated with inferior OS (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.15-1.78; p = 0.001), RFS (HR 1.48; p = 0.001), and LRC (HR 1.40; p = 0.018). High LNR/ENE-positive patients had significantly worse survival than the reference group, low LNR/ENE-negative (HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.47-2.95; p < 0.001). Low LNR/ENE-positive patients trended toward inferior survival (HR 1.36; p = 0.051), while high LNR/ENE-negative patients showed no significant difference (HR 1.12; p = 0.65). Conclusions: LNR is an independent prognostic factor beyond ENE across OS, RFS, and LRC in node-positive OCSCC. High LNR combined with ENE identifies a distinctly high-risk subgroup, whereas high LNR alone did not significantly impact survival in the absence of ENE. Incorporating LNR into postoperative risk stratification may refine identification of patients for risk-adapted adjuvant strategies.

items.title: Comparison of segment- and GTV-based target volume concepts in SBRT for vertebral metastases: a post hoc secondary analysis of two prospective clinical trials Target volume concepts in dose-escalation SBRT
items.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.authors: Madani I, Sweeney RA, Hawkins M, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To compare outcome of the segment-based and gross tumor volume (GTV)-based target volume definition concepts in fractionated SBRT for vertebral metastases. Material And Methods: This is a post hoc secondary analysis of two prospective clinical trials conducted between 2012 and 2015 (XXX1 [segment-based concept]) and between 2016 and 2023 (XXX2 [GTV-based concept]). In both trials, fractionated SBRT for painful and non-painful mechanically stable or potentially unstable vertebral metastases delivered two dose levels using simultaneous integrated boost (SIB): 35-40 Gy/5 or 48.5 Gy/10 to the high-dose planning target volume (PTV) and 20 Gy/5 and 30 Gy/10 to the conventional-dose PTV, respectively. The high-dose PTV was defined either as segment-based (XXX1) following international guidelines or GTV-based (XXX2). The primary endpoints were freedom from local progression (FFLP) and vertebral compression fracture (VCF) assessed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Results: Patient characteristics showed several imbalances, in general more favorable for patients in the XXX2 group. The high-dose PTV in the XXX2 group (177 patients with 197 metastases) was significantly smaller than in the XXX1 group (57 patients with 63 metastases) (median 11 cm3 vs median 58 cm3, P<.001). At median follow-up of survivors of 24 months, 2-year FFLP and progressive and de novo VCF rates in the XXX2 and XXX1 groups were 95.3% vs. 86.4% (P<.001) and 10.1% vs. 34.6% (P<.001), respectively. No myelopathy or plexopathy were observed in either group. On univariable analysis the segment-based concept (Hazard ratio [HR] 5.21, 95% CI 2.53-10.72; P<.001) and lumbar spine location (HR 2.44, 95% CI 1.24-4.82, P=.01) were associated with higher rates of progressive and de novo VCF. Conclusions: In fractionated SBRT for vertebral metastases, reduction of the high-dose PTV to the GTV combined with focal dose escalation and low-dose elective vertebral coverage did not compromise local control and lowered the rates of VCF.

items.title: Transoral robotic surgery for head and neck tumours: a critical systematic review of patient selection and outcome reporting
items.authors: Clay B, Crabtree P, Banham E, et al.
items.abstract: Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) is an emerging modality for the minimally invasive resection of head and neck tumours. Despite its introduction approximately 15 years ago, its use has not become widespread in clinical practice. It is hypothesised that both heterogenous patient selection and heterogenous reporting of safety, procedural efficiency,​oncological efficacy, and functional outcomes of TORS compared to alternative treatments has limited effective evidence synthesis and contributed to limited clinical adoption. This review aims to systematically assess patient selection and outcome reporting in the literature and identify areas for improvement. The Medline, Embase and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to June 2025. Articles were included if they reported TORS without neoadjuvant therapy for the management of any tumour in the head and neck, without restriction by subsite, stage, histological type, adjuvant therapy, or reported outcome(s). 1471 studies were identified from searches. After deduplication and screening, 70 studies were included, comprising one randomised controlled trial, 22 non-randomised comparative studies and 47 non-comparative studies. Participant inclusion criteria were generally well-defined according to tumour site and histopathological characteristics. Reporting of all outcomes across safety, oncological, functional and procedural domains was grossly heterogenous. Only six specific outcomes were reported by multiple comparative studies, four of which by the same two studies, which differed in fundamental disease characteristics. This study highlights the need for consistent reporting in TORS-based studies, possibly via a core outcome set, to facilitate robust evidence synthesis of the safety and efficacy of TORS.

items.title: Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic body radiotherapy with elective nodal irradiation for borderline resectable and unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer
items.authors: Umezawa R, Mizuma M, Nakagawa K, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Locoregional recurrence remains a major clinical challenge in borderline resectable (BR) and unresectable locally advanced (UR-LA) pancreatic cancer, even after stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). This phase I trial evaluated the safety, maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and preliminary efficacy of adding prophylactic elective nodal irradiation (ENI) to 5-fraction SBRT. Methods: Patients with BR/UR-LAPC were enrolled in a 3 + 3 dose-escalation design. SBRT was delivered in 5 fractions using either adaptive magnetic resonance image-guided radiation therapy or respiratory breath-hold radiotherapy with a fiducial marker. The ENI dose was fixed at 30 Gy in five fractions, while the primary tumor dose increased from Level 1 (35 Gy) to Level 3 (40 Gy). The primary endpoint was acute dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) (any Grade ≥ 3 non-hematological adverse events within 14 days after the completion of SBRT). Results: Twelve patients (BR: 4, LA: 8) were enrolled, 11 of whom had previously received systemic chemotherapy. One patient at Level 1 experienced acute Grade 3 anorexia/nausea requiring hospitalization. No DLTs were observed at Levels 2 and 3, and the MTD was not reached. Three patients with preexisting biliary stents developed subacute Grade 3 cholangitis. No Grade ≥ 3 late adverse events occurred. The median overall survival after SBRT was 17.3 months, and the 1-year locoregional control rate was 75%. Conclusion: Five-fraction SBRT with simultaneous 30 Gy ENI was feasible, and the MTD was not reached within the tested dose levels up to 40 Gy. Further prospective studies are needed to evaluate its long-term safety and treatment outcomes.

items.abstract: For indolent primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas (PCBCL), NCCN guidelines recommend a definitive radiation dose of 24 Gy for solitary/regional disease, and lower doses (as low as 4 Gy) for focal palliation but acknowledges that data is limited. We hypothesize that while 4 Gy may provide palliative benefit, re-treatment may be higher than previously reported and higher doses may result in more durable response. This study analyzes clinical outcomes for PCBCL lesions receiving 4, 8, or 12 Gy.

items.title: Tumor Treating Fields and Quality of Life Among Patients With Locally Advanced Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial
items.authors: Macarulla T, Picozzi V, Chandana SR, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: The PANOVA-3 trial demonstrated the survival benefit and tolerability of Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) therapy concomitant with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, but understanding the impact of TTFields therapy on quality of life (QoL) and pain is important for clinical decision-making. Objective: To analyze the impact of TTFields therapy concomitant with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel on QoL and pain outcomes using prospective data from PANOVA-3. Design, Setting, And Participants: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of PANOVA-3, which was a global, open-label, multicenter, phase 3 randomized clinical trial in adult patients with previously untreated locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma (LA-PAC). A total of 571 patients were randomized between May 1, 2018, and March 31, 2023, with follow-up completed October 31, 2024. Data analysis was performed from November 2024 to May 2025. Intervention: Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive either TTFields therapy (150 kHz) with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel or gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel alone. Nab-paclitaxel (125 mg/m2) and gemcitabine (1000 mg/m2) were administered intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of 28-day cycles. Duration of follow-up was 18 months. Main Outcomes And Measures: QoL was measured using the European Organization for the Research and Treatment of Cancer Core Quality of Life Questionnaire and the 26-item pancreatic cancer module. End points were mean changes from baseline QoL scores, deterioration-free survival of QoL, and time to opioid use. An analysis of pain medication use was performed post hoc. Results: At baseline, 562 patients (median [IQR] age, 67 [31-90] years; 295 [52.5%] female), including 279 of 285 patients in the TTFields plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel arm and 283 of 286 patients in the gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel arm, completed the EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire. Global health status was stable during the 26-month follow-up in both study arms. Digestive symptoms, pain, and pancreatic pain were improved from 2 months after treatment initiation throughout treatment and follow-up in the TTFields plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel arm. TTFields plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel was associated with longer deterioration-free survival for global health status than gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel alone (median [IQR], 7.1 [3.5-14.8] vs 5.7 [2.3-11.5] months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.77; 95% CI, 0.61-0.97; P = .02).…

items.title: Clinician Training, Text Messages, and Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Among Children Aged 10 to 12 Years: A Randomized Clinical Trial
items.authors: Staras SAS, Bylund CL, Gurka MJ, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates among adolescents remain below recommendations. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of clinician communication training and parent-targeted text messages at increasing HPV vaccination among children aged 11 to 12 years. Design, Setting, And Participants: This doubly randomized, 2-level nested clinical trial was conducted from February 2022 to September 2024 among clinicians at 30 pediatric primary care clinics in Florida, children aged 10 to 12 years who had not received any of the 3 adolescent HPV vaccines, and their parents. Interventions occurred for 1 year, and vaccine records were collected for 2 years. Interventions: Clinics were randomized 1:1:1 to 3 training groups: (1) the bundled approach, which presents the HPV vaccine in the middle of 2 other recommended vaccines; (2) the focused approach, which emphasizes cancer prevention; and (3) deferred, which offered clinicians the opportunity to participate in the focused training after the trial concluded. Clinicians in the first 2 groups completed a 1-hour communication training and a 5-minute booster session. Patients within clinics were randomized 1:1:1 to 3 text message groups, aligned with the communication strategies: (1) bundled, (2) focused, and (3) no text messages. Parents were sent text messages at the start of the study or prior to their child's 11th birthday as well as prior to appointments. Main Outcomes And Measures: Primary outcomes were HPV vaccine initiation (receipt of first dose) and completion (receipt of second dose). Analyses accounted for clinic-level clustering. Effects were analyzed as randomized and text messages as received. Results: At baseline, 59 clinicians (44 [75%] female; 12 [20%] Asian, 21 [36%] Hispanic, and 21 [36%] non-Hispanic White) within 30 randomized clinics were included, with 17 randomized to the focused group, 21 to the bundled group, and 21 to the deferred group. A total of 7234 children were aged 10 (3576 [49%]), 11 (2617 [36%]), and 12 (1041 [14%]) years at study start (1673 [23%] Hispanic, 1001 [14%] non-Hispanic Black, and 1210 [17%] non-Hispanic White). A total of 28 clinics (93%), 50 clinicians (85%), and 6498 children (90%) completed the 2-year follow-up. The mean pre-post clinic-level difference for HPV vaccine initiation was 28.2 (95% CI, 25.3-31.1) percentage points and for completion was 16.1 (95% CI, 13.3-18.9) percentage points. Risk ratios for clinician training and text messaging did not differ between groups for initiation or completion.…

items.title: TTA-MVUM: A Tumor and Text-Aware Multi-View Mamba Framework for Clinical Target Volume Auto-Segmentation in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Radiotherapy
items.journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.authors: Ma X, Wu R, Yi J, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Accurate segmentation of clinical target volumes (CTV) is critical for the success of radiotherapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Manual contouring is time-consuming and prone to considerable inter-observer variability. Current auto-segmentation models rely exclusively on images, which may lead to sub-optimal accuracy. This study sought to substantially improve CTV auto-segmentation by incorporating tumor and clinical text information with multimodal deep learning. Methods And Materials: We retrospectively collected data from 184 NPC patients treated at our institution, with 144 cases allocated for model training and 40 for test. We propose a tumor- and text-aware multi-view UMamba (TTA-MVUM) model with text-image cross-attention modules to fuse visual and textual features. The model input comprised CT images, manually contoured primary gross tumor volume and metastatic lymph nodes, structured text contouring plan extracted by a large language model from electronic health records. Training was guided by a composite loss integrating Dice, cross-entropy and contrastive terms. Model performance was evaluated using Dice, 95% Hausdorff distance and averaged surface distance. Results: The proposed TTA-MVUM model significantly outperformed state-of-the-art image-only and tumor-aware baselines, yielding mean Dice of 0.892 ± 0.035 for high-risk CTV, 0.738 ± 0.149 for low-risk CTV, and 0.889 ± 0.024 for the entire CTV, respectively, with similar improvements for other metrics. Using either tumor information or clinical text alone also surpassed baseline models, but performance remained inferior to the combined approach. Conclusions: Integrating tumor priors and text guidance can substantially improve the NPC CTV auto-segmentation accuracy and clinical applicability.

items.title: daNIS-2: a phase III, randomized, double-blind study of the anti-TGF-β monoclonal antibody NIS793 or placebo in combination with nab-paclitaxel/gemcitabine as first-line treatment in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
items.authors: Paulson S, Ikeda M, Shen L, et al.
items.abstract: Background: This phase III, randomized, double-blind study (daNIS-2) evaluated the efficacy and safety of NIS793, an anti-transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) monoclonal antibody, in combination with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel [standard of care (SOC)] versus placebo and SOC as first-line treatment in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (mPDAC). Patients And Methods: The study included a safety run-in (n = 21 patients enrolled) followed by a randomized part (n = 490 patients randomly assigned). Patients were assigned 1 : 1 to receive NIS793 or placebo with SOC. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), overall response rate (ORR), safety, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory biomarker analyses. Results: The study was terminated early following an interim analysis due to an unfavorable benefit-risk profile. Median OS was 9.2 months in the NIS793 arm versus 11.2 months in the placebo arm (hazard ratio 1.26, 95% confidence interval 1.01-1.59). The estimates of ORR and median PFS indicate a less favorable treatment effect with NIS793. Safety profiles were comparable between arms, although higher rates of anemia, epistaxis, and rash were observed with NIS793; serious adverse events were more frequent in the NIS793 arm, with most being grade ≥3. Pharmacodynamic markers such as Pro-C3 supported target engagement. However, such target engagement did not translate into clinical benefit and early circulating tumor DNA dynamics were associated with less favorable outcomes. Biomarker analyses suggested that unfavorable benefit-risk profile of NIS793 was most pronounced in patients with a low epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition signature and a classical molecular subtype. Conclusions: NIS793 in combination with SOC did not improve survival outcomes in first-line mPDAC and was associated with an unfavorable benefit-risk profile. Exploratory biomarker findings highlight the complexity of TGF-β signaling and underscore the need for refined patient selection strategies in future trials.

items.title: Pre-operative stereotactic radiosurgery versus intraoperative cesium-131 brachytherapy for resected brain metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.authors: Kite T, Mahmoudi DA, Singh E, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Pre-operative stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and intraoperative cesium-131 (Cs-131) brachytherapy are alternatives to post-operative SRS for resected brain metastases (BMs). The randomized phase 3 Radiation One and Done Study (ROADS; NCT04365374) showed improved surgical-bed control with Cs-131 tiles versus post-operative stereotactic radiotherapy, but outcomes relative to pre-operative SRS are undefined. Methods: PubMed, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched through October 2026 (PRISMA 2020); one further trial was identified by other methods. Twelve-month local control (LC), leptomeningeal disease (LMD), radiation necrosis (RN), and overall survival (OS) were extracted for treatment-naïve BMs. Proportions were pooled with random-effects generalized linear mixed models and compared with a test for subgroup differences; sensitivity analyses included meta-regression, Hartung-Knapp, leave-one-out, follow-up, and fractionation analyses. Results: Fifteen pre-operative SRS studies (918 patients/940 BMs) and four brachytherapy studies (207 patients/217 BMs) were included. Pooled 12-month LC was 97% (95% CI 90-99) with Cs-131 brachytherapy and 90% (86-93) with pre-operative SRS (test for subgroup differences p = 0.054; meta-regression p = 0.019; Hartung-Knapp p = 0.066); among studies reporting observed counts, LC was 99% vs. 90% (p = 0.009). Within pre-operative SRS, LC was 96% after hypofractionated and 86% after single-fraction treatment (p = 0.005). LMD (9.1% vs. 5.1%) and RN (0.7% vs. 5.2%) did not differ significantly. Median OS was 15.6 months with brachytherapy (range 5.9-42.5; 11.0 months, range 5.9-20.1, excluding the ROADS estimate) and 14.4 months with pre-operative SRS (range 6.3-26.4). Conclusion: Both approaches achieved high LC with low rates of LMD and RN. There was a trend towards higher LC with Cs-131 brachytherapy than with pre-operative SRS (97% vs. 90%; p = 0.054), and significantly so among studies reporting observed counts (99% vs. 90%; p = 0.009). Hypofractionated pre-operative SRS achieved LC similar to that of brachytherapy, suggesting that the difference may reflect single-fraction dose de-escalation rather than an intrinsic advantage of either modality. The two techniques may serve complementary roles, and prospective comparative study is warranted. Registration: This review was not registered in PROSPERO.
